rows.question: Is a gift of a house to my daughter valid if it is only written on plain paper, and does it need registration?
queries: Is a gift of a house to my daughter valid if it is only written on plain paper, and does it need registration?
gift of immovable property house transfer without registered instrument valid
The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 section 122 gift of immovable property
The Registration Act, 1908 section 17 documents of immovable property compulsory registration
topSources: The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 s122
The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 s123
The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 s129
rows.answer:
A gift of immovable property, such as a house, cannot be made through a writing on plain paper alone, because for the purpose of making a gift of immovable property, the transfer must be effected by a registered instrument signed by or on behalf of the donor and attested by at least two witnesses, as required by Section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 [3]. Furthermore, under Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908, instruments of gift of immovable property must be registered [2].

Conditions and time limits:
- The acceptance of the gift must be made during the lifetime of the donor and while the donor is still capable of giving, as provided in Section 122 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 [1].
- If the donee dies before acceptance, the gift is void, according to Section 122 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 [1].
- The document relating to immovable property must contain a description sufficient to identify the property, as set out in Section 21 of the Registration Act, 1908 [7].

Related provisions:
- Section 18 of the Registration Act, 1908 lists documents of which registration is optional [4].

rows.question: My employer sacked me without notice and has not paid my gratuity after five years. What are my rights?
queries: My employer sacked me without notice and has not paid my gratuity after five years. What are my rights?
termination of service without notice retrenchment compensation industrial disputes act
payment of gratuity eligibility continuous service of five years calculation
Industrial Disputes Act 1947 section 25F conditions precedent to retrenchment
topSources: The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 s4
The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 s2
rows.answer:
Gratuity is payable to an employee on the termination of employment after rendering continuous service for not less than five years on superannuation, retirement, resignation, death, or disablement due to accident or disease, as provided under Section 4 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 [2]. When a workman is asked to leave forthwith, he has to be paid at the time when he is asked to go and cannot be asked to collect his dues afterwards, as noted in the Supreme Court judgment National Iron and Steel Co. Ltd. & Ors. versus The State of West Bengal & Anr. [11].

Conditions and time limits:
- The employee must have rendered continuous service for not less than five years, except where termination is due to death or disablement [2].
- The employer must arrange to pay the amount of gratuity within thirty days from the date it becomes payable under Section 7 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 [8].

Related provisions:
- Section 7 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 covers the determination and payment of gratuity, including simple interest for delayed payments [8].

Furthermore, every police officer or other person arresting someone without a warrant must forthwith communicate full particulars of the offence or other grounds for the arrest, under Section 47 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, and previously Section 50 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 [1][8].

rows.question: Can I get a divorce on the ground of cruelty, and can I or my spouse claim maintenance while the case is going on?
queries: Can I get a divorce on the ground of cruelty, and can I or my spouse claim maintenance while the case is going on?

Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act section 20 monetary reliefs maintenance
topSources: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 s20
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence s20
rows.answer:
You can seek a divorce on the ground of cruelty, and either spouse can claim maintenance while the case is pending under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, Section 27(1)(d) of the Special Marriage Act, 1954, and Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 [1][2][7]. 

- Conditions and time limits:
- Under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, the applicant (either the wife or the husband) must show that she or he has no independent income sufficient for her or his support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding [2].
- The application for the payment of expenses and monthly maintenance during the proceeding shall, as far as possible, be disposed of within sixty days from the date of service of notice on the wife or the husband [2].

rows.question: A shop sold me a defective mobile phone. Does the law say goods must be fit for use, and where can I complain?
queries: A shop sold me a defective mobile phone. Does the law say goods must be fit for use, and where can I complain?

Consumer Protection Act 2019 remedy for defective goods
rows.answer:
The admissibility of the complaint shall ordinarily be decided within twenty-one days from the date on which the complaint was filed, under Section 36 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [9]. 

Conditions and time limits:
- The complaint may be filed with a District Commission electronically or in the manner prescribed, accompanied by the prescribed fee, under Section 35 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [1].
- The issue of admissibility shall ordinarily be decided within twenty-one days from the date of filing, and if not decided within that period, it shall be deemed to have been admitted under Section 36 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [9].

Related provisions:
- Section 36 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 covers the proceedings before the District Commission on receipt of a complaint [9].

I couldn't find an explicit statement in the searched Acts that goods must be "fit for use," but the Consumer Protection Act defines a "defect" as any fault, imperfection, or shortcoming in quality, quantity, potency, purity, or standard required by law or contract under Section 2 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 [2] and Section 2 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [3].

rows.answer:
Section 316 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which is the current law in force from 1 July 2024 and has replaced Section 406 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (previously Section 406 of the Indian Penal Code), provides that whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both [1][5]. 

Related provisions:
- Section 316(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which covers whoever, being entrusted with property as a carrier, wharfinger or warehouse-keeper, commits criminal breach of trust in respect of such property [1].
- Section 316(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which covers whoever, being a clerk or servant or employed as a clerk or servant, and being in any manner entrusted in such capacity with property, commits criminal breach of trust [1].
- Section 316(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which covers criminal breach of trust by a public servant or in the way of business as a banker, merchant, factor, broker, attorney or agent [1].

rows.question: What is the BNS offence of causing death by negligence, and which IPC section was it earlier?
queries: What is the BNS offence of causing death by negligence, and which IPC section was it earlier?
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita section 106 causing death by negligence
Indian Penal Code section 304A causing death by negligence
causing death by negligence rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide
topSources: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 s531
rows.answer:
Section 106 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is the current law in force, and it replaced Section 304A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, which is the old law [1][8].

- Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine [1].
- If the rash or negligent act is done by a registered medical practitioner while performing a medical procedure, the punishment is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and also a fine [1].
- If someone causes the death of any person by rash and negligent driving of a vehicle not amounting to culpable homicide, and escapes without reporting it to a police officer or a Magistrate soon after the incident, the punishment is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and also a fine [1].

Yes, dowry death is still an offence under Section 80 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which is the current law (in force from 1 July 2024), having replaced Section 304B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, the old law [1][9].

Conditions and time limits:
- The death of the woman must be caused by burns or bodily injury or occur otherwise than under normal circumstances [1][9].
- The death must occur within seven years of her marriage [1][9].

- Section 118 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, which is the current law (in force from 1 July 2024) and replaced Section 113B of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, covers the presumption as to dowry death [2][6][10].

Alternatively, a Magistrate may, at any stage of hearing of an application for a protection order or for any other relief under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, grant temporary custody of any child or children to the aggrieved person or the person making an application on her behalf, and specify, if necessary, the arrangements for the visit of such child or children by the respondent, under Section 21 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 [2]. If the Magistrate is of the opinion that any visit of the respondent may be harmful to the interests of the child or children, the Magistrate shall refuse to allow such visit, under Section 21 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 [2].

The police must forthwith communicate full particulars of the offence or other grounds of arrest and give information regarding the arrest and the place where the arrested person is held to a relative, friend, or nominated person under Section 47 and Section 48 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (which replaced Section 50 and Section 50A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, respectively) [1][4][5][10].

Conditions and time limits:
- The communication of grounds of arrest must be made forthwith upon an arrest without warrant under Section 47 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (previously Section 50 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973) [1][5].

queries: My son took over my house and now ignores me and my wife. Can we cancel the transfer?

topSources: The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 s126

rows.answer:
Yes, a senior citizen who has transferred property by way of gift or otherwise subject to the condition that the transferee shall provide basic amenities and basic physical needs, and where the transferee refuses or fails to provide them, may at their option have the transfer declared void by the Tribunal under Section 23 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 [2][11]. 

As expounded in the Supreme Court judgment of Urmila Dixit versus Sunil Sharan Dixit and Ors., attracting the application of Section 23(1) requires two conditions: (a) the transfer must have been made subject to the condition that the transferee shall provide the basic amenities and basic physical needs to the transferor, and (b) the transferee refuses or fails to provide such amenities and physical needs [11]. Furthermore, a donor and donee may agree that a gift shall be suspended or revoked on the happening of any specified event not depending on the donor's will under Section 126 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 [1].

Information Technology Act 2000 section 66D punishment for cheating by personation by using computer resource
topSources: The INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY ACT, 2000 Amendment s66D
The Information Technology Act, 2000 (Central Act 21 of 2000) s66D
rows.answer:
Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource cheats by personating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees under Section 66D of the Information Technology Act, 2000 [2].

Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly makes use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to rupees one lakh under Section 66C of the Information Technology Act, 2000 [1].

rows.answer:
Section 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides that whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any words, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object in any form, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and also with fine [5]. This provision is the current law (in force from 1 July 2024); it replaced section 509 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 [10].
